cards.headline: NNPC eyes 10% equity sale, London, New York listings
cards.what_happened: NNPC is considering selling a 10% equity stake in itself and pursuing listings on the London and New York stock exchanges.
analysis: Why it matters: A partial sale and foreign listings would change the shareholding structure of Nigeria's state oil company, which is relevant to public ownership transparency. The source text contains only a headline, so the scope and terms are unconfirmed.
cards.ownership_caveat: Ownership details as reported by Punch; not verified with CAC records.

cards.headline: Ibori loses appeal over £102million corrupt assets forfeiture
cards.what_happened: James Ibori has lost an appeal against the forfeiture of corrupt assets valued at £102 million. The ruling upholds the seizure of assets linked to his conviction for corruption while he was Delta State governor.
analysis: As reported by Premium Times; AURA has not checked court or agency records. An allegation or charge is not a finding of guilt.

cards.headline: Reps invite CBN governor over alleged unpaid pensions arrears |
cards.byline: The Eagle Online · Tue 3 Nov, 19:58 Lagos
cards.what_happened: The House of Representatives resolved to invite CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso to explain alleged breaches of pension agreements and unpaid benefits to retired central bank employees. The House also mandated its Committee on Pension to investigate alleged non-compliance, unpaid arrears and the exclusion of pensioners from general pension increases.
key_facts: The House mandated its Committee on Pension to investigate alleged CBN non-compliance with pension agreements.
CBN pensioners declined from 5,104 in 2011 to approximately 3,000, a reduction of more than 2,100.
The House urged the CBN to verify and pay all outstanding arrears within a reasonable, clearly defined period.
analysis: As reported by The Eagle Online; AURA has not checked court or agency records. An allegation or charge is not a finding of guilt.

cards.headline: PIA reforms lift oil output by 600,000bpd — NNPC
cards.what_happened: The NNPC says reforms under the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) have lifted Nigeria's oil output by 600,000 barrels per day. The statement credits the regulatory changes for the production increase. The report contains no details on specific companies, ownership changes or contracts.
analysis: Why it matters: The PIA reform framework shapes the operating environment for upstream oil companies and the public revenue they generate. The article reports no ownership or procurement change.
